attack-order.text:
# Attack Order
Each player’s characters attack in left-to-right, front-to-back order, starting with the top-left "Slot 1".
Characters attack enemies at random, with enemy front row characters protecting their back row.
= 401px)"/>
By default, the player who gets the first attack is random. Some effects (like Warp Drive Engine) grant a player the first attack. If both players have such effects, they may cancel each other out (or stack when duplicated).
## Notes
- Characters attack a random front row enemy if possible, unless the attacker has Sneak.
- Ranged characters deal damage without taking damage back.
- If a character is summoned mid-fight, the slot it is summoned into determines its attack order. (If it enters a slot that just attacked, it will be granted the next attack).

banking-characters.text:
# Banking Characters
“Banking” is a special mechanic in Galaxy that allows you to recruit a character from the shop without replacing another character on your board. Dragging a shop character into the top-left bank slot gives all effects from recruiting it, but it does not participate in fights.
= 401px)"/>
## Notes
- You cannot bank a character from the shop until you have filled up your board.
- Banking a character triggers all of its recruit abilities, including any drawbacks (looking at you, Prince Charming, the Heartbreaker!).
- Banking a bronze character counts as finding your first copy. The next time you see that character in the shop, it will be silver.
- Banking a silver character will trigger its inherent Bonus Shop, and the next time you see that character in the shop, it will be golden.
- Banking a golden character will trigger its inherent Treasure Shop, and the card will be removed from the card pool.
- Quest characters must be on your board to progress and complete their quests.
- Banking a quest character from the shop without a copy on your board will not trigger its own quest.

board.text:
# Board
Your board consists of 5 slots that hold characters: three in the front row (top) and two in the back row (bottom). A Bank slot in the top-left corner allows recruiting characters without placing them on your board.
Slots themselves can be buffed, which stay even if the character positioned there changes (see Slot Buffs).
Slots can also be painted to apply color-based effects.
## Notes
- Slots are colloquially referred to in numeric order starting with "Slot 1" in the top-left and going left → right, front → back
- When an effect refers to your "first slot" or "first character" it means the slot in the top-left, regardless of whether or not the slot has a character in it (for example, Dracula’s Fangs).
- See Attack Order for details on how your characters’ positions on-board determine their attack sequence.

boons.text:
# Boons
Boons are special treasures with powerful effects and special rules.
Boons are not acquired like normal treasures, they are not rewarded for taking golden characters or completing Quests. Boons are gained through cards’ effects, such as Orpheus giving Boons if you have a cracked heart.
Boons have a condition, similar to Quests, which must be met before you get their effects.
## Notes
- Boons reward other cards or play powerful spells. After gaining a Boon’s reward, it disappears (it no longer counts towards Treasure Hoard).
- Unfinished Boons you already have cannot be options in new Boon discovery shops. You can rediscover Boons after they’ve been completed, and complete them again.
- Boons are treasures, they are affected by treasure-copying or treasure-stealing effects.
- Boons were introduced in Galaxy’s third set, Mythbound: Prophecies of the Nether Realm.

bronze-characters.text:
# Bronze Characters
The first time you see a character in your shop, it will be bronze -- showing that you have not recruited it yet. All characters start at Bronze and do not have any additional inherent bonuses from being bronze.
## Notes
- The second copy of a character you recruit is Silver
- The third copy of a character you recruit is Golden.

buffs.text:
# Buffs
In Galaxy, buffs are usually permanent. Once a character buff increases its attack or health, it keeps that buff for the rest of the game.
The buff will apply in all future fights, and future copies of that character (such as Silvers or Goldens) include that buff when they appear in the shop.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- If you buff a character during a fight, it keeps those buffs when you return to the shop.
- If you summon a character during a fight and buff it (for example, summoning a character with Goodie Bag), the summoned character retains the buff when summoning it again in a future fight or seeing it in the shop.
- If you transform a character into a new one, the new character retains all the buffs from the original.
- Buffs to card abilities are also permanent, and carried on through transformations. For example: if the +1/+1 ability on Snow Ball is buffed up to +6/+6, then Snowball is transformed into Frankenstein, Frankenstein’s ability would give +7/+7 instead of +2/+2.
- Slot buffs to your board are permanent. Since they are tied to the slot and not the character, they remain if the character there changes.
## Auras
- Some card abilities improve characters’ stats without giving a permanet buff. These "aura" effects are worded in a way where the card needs to be on your board in order to provide the buff.
- Most support abilities are aura effects.
- Since these effects are constantly checking, if the condition is changed or the character is removed, those effects no longer apply.
- For example, Moonshadow grants other support characters Ranged. When Moonshadow is KO’d, those characters lose Ranged.

candy.text:
# Candy
Candy is a card super-type that appears on characters, treasures, and spells. Candy cards’ effects can be "sweetened" throughout the game to increase their bonuses.
## Sweetening Candy
The first time an effect "sweetens your Candy", a Candy Counter appears to track your sweetness. It starts at 1, increasing further whenever you sweeten.
Sweetness affects all your Candy cards’ buff effects (e.g +2 Attack, +5 Health, +4/+4) as a direct +1/+1 increase to those stats.
For example, an effect that normally buffs a character by +1/+1 would give it +5/+5 instead if your Candy is sweetened to 4.
### Supersweet
The Supersweet keyword enhances Candy bonuses further, by multiplying the effect’s sweet-bonus by the Supersweet value.
## Deckbuilding with Candy
Most Candy characters are collectible. Aside from a handful Candy cards in the shared-pool and characters with "All" types (such as Catamari), you typically only interact with the Candy mechanic if you choose to include Candy characters in your deck.
Candy spells appear if you include at least 1 Candy card in your deck (or play a Candy-based captain).
## Notes
- Candy cards are identifiable by their special card frames and banners.
- Cards may become Candy through various effects (and their buffs would then be sweetened). A gained the Candy type is passed it along when a character is transformed.
- Candy is the namesake mechanic from Galaxy’s second set, Candylar: The Sweet Set.

captains.text:
# Captain
Captains are the champions of Galaxy, and your partners as you journey throughout the magical worlds. Before each game begins you select one Captain for the game, and one of their decks to shuffle into the shared card pool.
New premium captains are released each month. They all automatically become FREE for all players 2 months after their release.
## Notes
- Most captains begin the game with 3 full hearts (see Heart Damage).
- Each captain has their own collection of collectible cards that you unlock through playing.
## Cosmetics
- After unlocking 50 collectible cards for a captain, you gain their Diamond frame to show off your mastery of that captain.
- "Costumes" are available for each captain, letting you change their look with alternate-artworks or variants that change the original art’s look.
- Frame banners change the bottom half of the captain’s frame.

chance-encounter.text:
# Chance Encounter
A Chance Encounter ability triggers whenever the card appears in the shop.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Chance Encounter was introduced in Galaxy’s fourth set, Chromaria.

characters.text:
# Characters
Characters are the primary card type in Galaxy that you interact with each turn. Characters are gained by recruiting them from the shop to your board.
Characters fight one another in the fight phase, each dealing damage using their Attack (the number on the left) and receiving damage against their Health (the number on the right). When a character’s health reaches 0, they are KO’d and you will see them again when you return to the shop.
Most characters have ability text that gives them special bonuses throughout the game - see these by zooming on the card.
Each character has a rarity, shown by the gem at the bottom of their card frame. This determines when it starts appearing in the shop and what treasure it finds when goldened.
Gem-icons for each rarity
## Notes
- Characters can have one or more faction types, which are displayed on the card’s frame on zoom.
- Recruiting a character consists of dragging it from the shop to your board or to the bank.
- The second time you see a character in the shop it will be Silver and recruiting it will grant you a Bonus Shop.
- The third time you see a character in the shop it will be Golden and recruiting it will grant you a Bonus Treasure Shop.

decks.text:
# Decks
Galaxy decks consist of 12 collectible cards.
Before a game starts, after selecting the captain you choose which deck to use. The deck’s 12 cards are shuffled into the shared pool to generate your custom card pool for the game. Collectible cards that are not in your deck will not show up for you during the game.
= 181px)"/>
## Deckbuilding
Each captain comes with 12 cards that make up their "Starter Deck", designed to work well with that captain’s strategy.
After unlocking the 13th+ card for a captain, may edit the starter deck and create your own custom deck. By swapping collectible cards in and out of these decks, you will see a slightly different pool of cards in your shops.
= 181px)"/>
## Theme Decks
Captains also have a pre-designed 12-card theme decks which are available for purchase. When buying a theme deck, all its cards are immediately be added to your collection for that captain and may be used in any of its decks.
Theme decks are prices based on its unowned cards. The gem price automatically reduces as more cards are collected. If you already own all 12 cards, the deck will be free.
## Notes
- Each captain has their own collection, which can all be unlocked for free as you play.
- Your opponents have their own custom card pools with their 12-card decks - pools are not shared between players in the game.
- The deck gets shuffled randomly into the shared pool - there are no increased odds of seeing a collectible card vs. a shared pool card of the same rarity during a game.

factions.text:
# Factions
There are various character types across Galaxy (colloquially called "factions"). Characters may have one faction, more than one faction, or even "ALL" factions. You can see which factions a character is by zooming on the card. These factions are an important part of the strategy of the game as many special abilities refer to specific factions.
## Major Factions

farewell.text:
# Farewell
A Farewell ability triggers when a character is KO’d.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- The Farewell ability triggers on KO regardless of whether the character was the attacker or not.
- A character must have a Farewell ability for this to trigger—just getting KO’d isn’t enough.
- If the Farewell ability creates one or more summons, the first summon will be created in the same slot where the Farewell character was.

fight.text:
# Fight
The fight is one of the two phases of your turn during a game of Galaxy (the other being the Shop phase). Fights occur against another opponent in your lobby. At the conclusion of the fight, the losing player will take Heart Damage based on the result of the fight, and you will proceed to the next Shop phase until you are the last one standing or run out of hearts.
See Attack Order for details on how characters sequence attacks during a fight.
= 401px)"/>

golden-characters.text:
# Golden Characters
After recruiting the second copy of a character, you may see that character again in one of your shops. This third copy will be Golden. By recruiting the golden copy, its stats will naturally be +1/+1 larger, and will give you a Bonus Shop full of treasures.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- The Treasure shop will be the same rarity as the character that was goldened.
- Turning the character golden will remove it from the card pool for the rest of the game.
- Many characters (but not all) will have their abilities doubled when turned golden. You can see these by selecting “Golden” in the cards database.
- Banking a golden character is the same as recruiting it and will still give you the Treasure shop.
- If the silver copy is on your board, the golden copy will automatically replace it.
- If you turn something golden using a spell (like Midas Touch), you do not gain the buff or the Treasure Shop.
- If the character has a “When you golden me” effect (e.g., Nameless One), it will still trigger, whether you recruit the golden copy from the shop or turn it golden using a targeted effect.

heart-damage.text:
# Heart Damage
Each player starts with 3 hearts. Players are eliminated from the game when they run out of hearts.
Damaging a heart will either crack it or empty it. Cracked hearts may be healed, but emptied hearts are permanent.
Heart damage is determined by the results of each fight:
- If you lose:
- If the opponent has 2 or fewer characters left, you crack one heart. Already-cracked hearts are emptied.
- If the opponent has 3 or more characters left, your heart is emptied, regardless of whether is started full or cracked.
- In the finals, when only 2 players remain, each loss always empties a heart.
- If you win a fight while you have a cracked heart, it is healed to full.
- Some effects give bonus hearts, such as Lich King's Heart.

hunt.text:
# Hunt
A Hunt ability triggers when a character attacks and KO’s an enemy.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- The character with the Hunt ability needs to be the attacker for the Hunt to trigger.
- The defending character must be KO’d for the Hunt to trigger.
- If the attacker is KO’d while Hunting, the ability will still trigger.
- A character only "hunts" if they have a Hunt ability. A character without Hunt simply attacking and KO’ing an enemy does not constitute a hunt.
- Certain cards grant a hunt ability onto characters while they are on board, like Tsarmina, the Tyrant.

paint.text:
# Paint
The Paint mechanic applies colors to your board’s slots to give them ongoing effects.
Paint changes a slot visually, applying the color and giving it a bonus +1/+1 slot buff.
## Colors and Effects
Paint has three primary colors: Red, Blue, and Yellow. Red and Yellow affect characters on their slots, growing their abilities every turn. Blue rewards you for playing spells.
Red slots
Buff character abilities here by +1 Attack each fight.
Yellow slots
Buff character abilities here by +1 Health each fight.
Blue slots
When you cast a spell, give this slot +1/+1.
Painting another color creates secondary colors, which combine and improve those effects.
Purple slots (Red + Blue)
Buff character abilities here by +2 Attack each fight. When you cast a spell, give this slot +2/+2.
Green slots (Blue + Yellow)
Buff character abilities here by +2 Health each fight. When you cast a spell, give this slot +2/+2.
Orange slots (Red + Yellow)
Buff character abilities here by +2/+2 Attack each fight.
Be careful, as paint cannot be removed or changed! As a rule, each slot only takes two colors — re-applying a color or painting the third only gives the bonus slot buff with no other effect.
Some cards break that rule, however, combining all three colors into Rainbow slots with more powerful effects!
Rainbow slots (Red + Blue + Yellow)
Buff character abilities here by +4/4 each fight. When you cast a spell, give this slot +4/+4.
## Deckbuilding with Paint
Most characters that enable or care about Paint are collectible. If you play these characters in your deck (or play a Paint-based captain), Paintbrush spells — which paint a slot their color — can appear in your shop.
Paintbrushes are only added for the colors your cards care about — if only Red and Yellow (or Orange) are referenced, the Blue Paintbrush will not appear.
## Notes
- Some cards’ abilities care about the color of their slot. For example, BaBaBanana is only active on a Yellow slot. Secondary-colored and rainbow slots count as all their colors.
- Paint’s bonus +1/+1 slot buff is part of the mechanic’s effect. Spell-buffing effects do not make Paintbrushes give a larger bonus.
- Paint was introduced in Galaxy’s fourth set, Chromaria.

prophecy.text:
# Prophecy
Prophecies are special abilities with a condition that must be met, similar to Quests. Unlike Quests, which reward treasures, when a Prophecy’s condition is completed you become a powerful captain!
## Notes
- When you become a prophesied captain, you keep your previous captain (they become a co-captain).
- Cards that copy your captain, such as and opponent’s Goat T or Boon of Styx, copy the Prophecy captain instead of your starting captain.
- Taking a golden character does not reward the captain (though you still get a treasure), you must complete the Prophecy’s condition to get it.
- Prophecy was introduced in Galaxy’s third set, Mythbound: Prophecies of the Nether Realm.

quest.text:
# Quests
Quests are special character abilities with a condition that must be met. When the condition is fulfilled, the quest is complete and the character gives you a bonus shop of treasures.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Most questers include a counter to show your progress.
- Questers must be on your board in order to track progress. For example, Shipshape Inspector must be placed on the board with 5 slot buffs - banking him will not complete the quest.
- Under normal circumstances, quests can only be completed once per character.
- Some quests require a number of characters be recruited (Evil Stepmother for example). If the quest character on-board only needs one more trigger, you can recruit directly onto its slot to complete the quest while replacing the quester.
- The bonus treasure shop for completing the quest is the same rarity as the quest character.

ranged.text:
# Ranged
When a ranged character attacks, they don't take damage back.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- This one-sided damage only occurs when the character with Ranged is the attacker.
- If a ranged character gets attacked by an enemy, damage will occur as normal.
- Some characters can grant the Ranged ability to other characters while they are on the board (see Moonshadow).
- Special cards (see Mimic) can gain Ranged permanently. If that character is then transformed, it will retain its Ranged ability.

rarity.text:
# Rarity
Most cards in Galaxy have a rarity, which can be identified by the color and shape of the gem in their card frame. Rarities serve a variety of purposes in the game, but the most common uses are: when a card can begin showing up in shops and what rarity treasure can be collected from a goldened or quest character. Characters, Treasures, and Spells have rarity.
Gem-icons for each rarity
There is also a rumored "Secret Rare" that can be found with special abilities.
## Notes
- The spell frame does not have a visual rarity gem, but spells do have rarity, which can be seen by zooming on the spell.
- The rarity of your current shop is denoted by the rarity symbol in the top-right of the shop near the turn number.

recruit.text:
# Recruit
A Recruit ability triggers when you take a card from the shop.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- A character with recruit will also trigger when recruiting the silver or golden copy of it.
- Banking a character is also considered recruiting and will trigger its Recruit ability.
- A Recruit ability specifically refers to abilities that start with the word "Recruit --" for effects such as Drafty Window.
- If you transform into a character with a recruit ability, it will not trigger (as it was not recruited from the shop).

shared-pool.text:
# Shared Pool
Shared pool cards are accessible to all players and can show up in every game of Galaxy. These cards are not collectible, and cannot be added to decks.
You can distinguish shared pool vs collectible cards in the collection tab from the lack of subtle filigree and banner color on the character frame.
The shared pool is updated from time-to-time, and come cards are added, retired, or re-balanced.

shop.text:
# Shop
The Shop is one of the two phases of your turn during a game of Galaxy (the other being the Fight). The shop normally consists of 3 characters. Each shop you have the option to choose one of the three characters to recruit by dragging it down onto your board (or to the bank). Starting on turn 3, a fourth choice, a Spell, is added to the shop. By default, you are presented with two shops per turn -- although there are various ways to increase this.
## Shop Leveling
When you start the game on Turn 1, your shop contains only Common rarity characters. Every other turn (Turns 1, 3, 5, 7, 9), your shop levels up, and the next rarity tier is shuffled into the shop pool. At any time you can see the rarity of your current shop as well as how many shops you have remaining this turn from the small rarity icons in the top-right corner of the screen near the turn counter.
Rarity |
Added to Shop |
Commons |
Turn 1 |
Uncommons |
Turn 3 |
Rares |
Turn 5 |
Epics |
Turn 7 |
Legendaries |
Turn 9 |
There have been rumors of a higher rarity (Secret Rare) that may be possible using special abilities.
## Bonus Shop
Some effects (most commonly by silvering a character) provide the player with a Bonus Shop. This is simply an additional shop for the player that turn at no cost. You can see how many shops you have remaining in a turn from the symbols in the top-right near the turn number.

silver-characters.text:
# Silver Characters
After recruiting the first copy of a character, you may see that character again in one of your shops. This second copy will be silver. By recruiting the silver copy, its stats will naturally be +1/+1 larger and will give you a Bonus Shop.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Banking a silver character is the same as recruiting it and will still give you the bonus shop.
- If the bronze copy is on your board, the silver copy will automatically replace it.
- If you turn something silver using a spell or effect (like Silvery Moon), you do not gain the Bonus Shop.
- If the character has a “When you silver me” effect (like Aladdin), it will still trigger, whether you recruit the silver copy from the shop or turn it silver using a targeted effect.

slot-buffs.text:
# Slot Buffs
Sometimes you may wish you could buff one of your characters, but want the buff to stick around even after swapping them out. That’s where Slot Buffs come in.
Some effects (such as Presence of Gaia) will specifically buff a "slot" on your board. This means the buff applies to one of your five board positions, not to the character itself. The buff stays on that slot no matter which character moves into it.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- You can pick up a character during your turn to quickly see which slot buffs are affecting that slot.
- If a slot currently has a slot buff, you’ll see a subtle green splat icon under the stats.
- If a targeted spell targets a slot, it also counts as targeting the character currently there (this matters for effects like Ironcast Dragon).

sneak.text:
# Sneak
Sneak characters attack the back row first.
= 181px)"/>
- If the Sneak character is the attacker, it will attempt to attack one of the two back row enemies (chosen randomly).
- If there are no back row enemies, the Sneak character will attack any character randomly.
- See attack order for a detailed sequence of how characters attack.

spells.text:
# Spells
Starting on Turn 3, your shop expands to include not only 3 characters but also 1 spell. Spells behave differently than characters as they have no stats, feature a distinct spell frame, and are one-time use only. To cast a spell, simply drag it down onto your board area (some spells have a specific target, while others do not).
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- To cast a spell that targets a specific character, drag it directly onto that character.
- If a spell specifies it targets a slot, drag it to the character currently in that slot. This still counts as casting the spell on a character (for effects like Ironcast Dragon).
- Casting a spell uses up your shop, you are choosing the spell instead of recruiting a character that turn.
- You cannot bank spells. If you’re granted a Bonus Spell, you must cast it. Be careful!
- While spells do not show rarity gems on their card frames, they do have rarities (which you can see on card zoom) and follow the same shop rarity progression as characters.
- Some spells only appear under specific circumstances. For example, Candy spells appear if you play with a Candy captain or Candy characters in your deck.

summon.text:
# Summon
A summon occurs when a character is created in the middle of the fight by another card’s effect.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Characters recruited from the shop during the shop phase are not considered summons.
- The slot the character summons into is the same slot as the source that summoned it (if that character was KO’d).
- If there is no space on the board, the summon will fail.
- A summoned character inherit the same attack priority as its source. If the character with the summon ability just attacked and was KO’d, the summoned character will get the next attack.
- Summoned cards are considered full cards, and any buffs applied to them during the fight is permanent. Those buffs stay when they are summoned again or you see them in the shop. Remember, "Summons keep their buffs!"
- Generally, characters may only be summoned if they are available in your shop, determined by your shop's level. A card summons a random character will not summon a rare on uncommon turns!

supersweet.text:
# Supersweet
Supersweet multiplies the effect your sweetness has on a Candy card’s stat-buffing effects by the supersweet value.
For example, if you have sweetened 0 times, Chubby Cheep buffs its slot by +3/+3 each fight. After you sweeten your Candy 9 times, Chubby Cheep buffs its slot by +30/+30 (+9/+9 sweetness × +3/+3 from Supersweet3 + original +3/+3 base buff).

support.text:
# Support
Support characters give a bonus to the characters in front of them.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Most support characters do not give a permanent buff and their support effect no longer applies if the support is KO’d (see the "Auras" section of buffs).
- Some supports (such as Moonshadow) also grant an ability with their support. This ability is also be removed when the support character is KO’d.
- Many cards with support are Fae. If an effect increases a "Fae Buff" - it is referring to the buff that card is providing (in this case, the support buff).

sweeten.text:
# Sweeten
Sweetening your Candy improves the buffs from ALL your Candy cards’ abilities by +1/+1.
For example, Gum Drop normally buffs a character by +1/+1. If your Candy is sweetened to 4, it gives +5/+5 instead.

transform.text:
# Transform
Transforming a character changes it into an entirely new character, while keeping any changes to its tier, buffs, and abilities.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Transforming keeps the tier (bronze/silver/golden) of the original character.
- After transforming, the original character is removed from the card pool and no longer appears in the shop. This does not apply to temporary transforms such as Medusa or Stroke of Midnight.
- Transforming keeps the buffs from the original character.
- Transforming a character whose ability was buffed (ex: Snow Ball) will keep those ability-buffs on the new character’s ability.
- Transforming a character mid-fight causes the new character to be "seen" as a new character when considering attack order.
- Transforming does not trigger recruit abilities (it was not recruited from the shop).

treasure-find.text:
# Treasure Find
The first treasure you collect from a character with Treasure Find is always the one specified in the ability.
## Notes
- The specified treasure always appears the first time the character discovers a treasures - whether from that character’s quest, from recruiting its golden copy, or any other means.
- The specified treasure is only offered once - it will not appear if the character discovers another treasure.
- Treasures found via Treasure Find are usually unique to that character and cannot be discovered any other way.
- The Treasure Find discovery replaces the default 3-choice selection with its unique treasure. Additional treasure discoveries work as normal.

treasure-hoard.text:
# Treasure Hoard
Treasure Hoard gives a character a +1/+1 buff for each treasure you have, multiplied by the Treasure Hoard count.
= 181px)"/>
## Notes
- Treasure Hoard is usually displayed with a number (Treasure Hoard 5 gives +5/+5 for each Treasure you have). If there is no number, the character has Treasure Hoard 1.
- Instances of Treasure Hoard are stackable - for example, casting Greed on a Dragonling gives it Treasure Hoard 2.
- Characters with Treasure Hoard in the shop show their correct stats with the buff already applied.

treasures.text:
# Treasures
Treasures are permanent bonuses that help you throughout a game of Galaxy. You earn them in various ways throughout the game and they exist only during the active game. The most common ways to earn treasures are by recruiting the golden (third copy) of a character or by completing a character’s quest.
When gaining treasures:
- "Discover" or "Choose" means selecting from a treasure shop with 3 choices.
- "Get" a treasure means automatically gaining it directly.
- "Collect" occurs any time a treasure is added - whether by selecting it or getting it directly.
## Notes
- After earning a large number of treasures, a treasure chest icon appears. Click it to see all your treasures.
- Treasures cannot usually be destroyed, unless by their own effects. There is maximum cap on collected treasures however, and gaining new treasures after that point removes older ones.
- Treasures discovered by characters match the rarity of the character that discovered them.
- The Treasure Hoard ability grants a character a +1/+1 buff for each Treasure you own.
